hero.name: Jinhong Yu
hero.thesis: I build the systems between people and robots: teleoperation, mixed-reality tools, and the capture rigs that turn human demonstrations into robot training data.
hero.intro: As the founding robotics engineer at Theta‑intelligence, I built a Meta Quest teleoperation platform with its real-time streaming layer, plus handheld and egocentric data-collection systems. My background is mechanical engineering and an M.S. in AI, so the work runs from CAD and wiring to Unity, perception and model fine-tuning.

experienceSection.title: Experience
experienceSection.intro: Robotics, XR and AI engineering, and most recently full-stack web.

points.text: Building an e-commerce platform: a store-management back office for merchants and a customer-facing WeChat Mini Program.

points.label: Teleoperation
points.text: Built the Meta Quest teleoperation app (Unity, OpenXR) with mixed-reality UI and external UVC camera support, and the real-time layer that streams video, audio and control between robots, headsets and remote operator stations.

points.label: Data collection
points.text: Designed and integrated the capture hardware, a Quest-tracked handheld UMI gripper and an egocentric rig, and built synchronized recording pipelines on Raspberry Pi and Quest for video, sensor and IoT data.

points.label: Edge AI
points.text: Wrote Android native plugins that run ONNX models on Quest, including sherpa-onnx text-to-speech, and deployed voice-driven AI agents on ESP32 (ESP-Claw) and Raspberry Pi (zero-Claw).
Fine-tuned Stable Diffusion on limited GPU hardware using LoRA and model parallelism.
Deployed a text-to-video pipeline aimed at multi-character scenes with consistent characters, and supported the team's text-to-image and text-to-video experiments.
Graded coursework, held office hours and gave a guest lecture on diffusion models.
Set up lab servers for research projects, and designed, implemented and ran experiments for project leads.
